source: NCERT Class XI, India Physical Environment, Ch. 7 (Natural Hazards and Disasters).

sections.heading: 1. Hazards and Disasters — Meaning
points: A **natural hazard** = a potential threat from a natural process; a **disaster** occurs when a hazard causes serious loss of life and property beyond a community's coping capacity.
Disasters are classified as **natural** (geological, atmospheric, hydrological, biological) and **man-made**.
**Disaster management** involves prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, recovery.

sections.heading: 2. Earthquakes and Tsunamis
points: **Earthquakes** — sudden ground shaking from energy release along faults; India divided into **seismic zones (II–V)**; the **Himalayas and NE** are high-risk (Zone V).
Measured by the **Richter scale (magnitude)** and **Mercalli scale (intensity)**.
**Tsunami** — huge sea waves from undersea earthquakes; the **2004 Indian Ocean tsunami** devastated coasts (Andaman, Tamil Nadu).

sections.heading: 3. Floods, Droughts and Cyclones
points: **Floods** — common in the Ganga-Brahmaputra plains (Assam, Bihar, WB); caused by heavy monsoon rain, silting, deforestation.
**Droughts** — deficient rainfall; types: meteorological, agricultural, hydrological; affect Rajasthan, interior Deccan.
**Cyclones** — tropical storms hitting the **east coast** (Bay of Bengal) more than the west; storm surges cause heavy damage (Odisha, Andhra, TN, WB).

sections.heading: 4. Landslides and Disaster Management
points: **Landslides** — downslope movement of rock/soil; common in the **Himalayas and Western Ghats** (steep slopes, heavy rain, deforestation).
**Disaster management** in India: the **Disaster Management Act (2005)**; the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** headed by the PM; **NDRF** (response force).
Focus is shifting from relief to **preparedness and mitigation**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Hazard = potential threat; disaster = actual serious damage beyond coping capacity.
Earthquakes: Richter (magnitude), Mercalli (intensity); Himalayas/NE = Zone V (highest risk).
Tsunami = undersea earthquake waves (2004 Indian Ocean tsunami).
Cyclones hit the east coast more (Bay of Bengal); floods in Ganga-Brahmaputra plains.
Disaster Management Act 2005; NDMA (headed by PM); NDRF.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Richter = magnitude (energy)**; **Mercalli = intensity (damage felt)**.
The **Himalayas and NE** are the **highest earthquake-risk (Zone V)** areas.
The **east coast (Bay of Bengal)** faces more cyclones than the west.
The **NDMA** is headed by the **Prime Minister** (Disaster Management Act, 2005).
